name: Harboring Anger
overview: Scripture warns against harboring anger in the heart, urging believers to avoid hatred and to confront sin lovingly rather than allowing it to fester (Leviticus 19:17). The wisdom literature highlights the value of patience and restraint, showing that a person who is slow to anger demonstrates understanding and promotes peace, while quick temper leads to folly and strife (Proverbs 14:29; 15:18). Believers are called to respond gently to anger with soft answers that turn away wrath, and to exercise discretion by deferring anger and choosing to overlook offenses as a mark of glory (Proverbs 15:1; 19:11). Ultimately, the faithful are exhorted to cease from anger and avoid wrath, recognizing the danger of allowing anger to lead to evil actions (Psalms 37:8).
